name: Projection Recoverability Limits Registry

core_rule.name: projection_non_recoverability_rule
core_rule.definition: A projection output cannot reconstruct its original ⇔R source relation unless external trace metadata preserves the lost aspect, residue, and source-relation context.

recoverability_classes.name: not_recoverable
recoverability_classes.definition: Projected form lacks sufficient source metadata for reconstruction.

recoverability_classes.name: trace_recoverable
recoverability_classes.definition: Projected form can point back to source relation through external trace metadata, but cannot internally reconstruct it.

recoverability_classes.name: partially_context_recoverable
recoverability_classes.definition: Projected form preserves enough metadata to recover some aspect roles, but not full simultaneity or residue-history.

recoverability_classes.name: restricted_whole_reference_recoverable
recoverability_classes.definition: Projected form preserves source pointer, aspect roles, and loss accounting sufficient to re-enter governed whole-relation analysis.

projection_recoverability_defaults.reason: Equality retains substitutability only; source relation requires external trace metadata.
Implication preserves direction only; simultaneity and mutuality are lost.
Composition preserves ordering only; indivisible co-presence is lost.
Biconditional preserves reciprocal truth readability only; residue-bound closure is lost.

forbidden_claims: Deep projection can serve as primitive evidence.
